title: Asymptotic ends and ADM surface integrals

items.title: A specified asymptotically Euclidean ADM end
items.design_state: Step 1 authoring complete draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.physical_scope: A fixed-chart geometric definition of an asymptotic energy limit; no Einstein constraint, positivity, coordinate-invariance, or empirical claim is included.
items.statement:
For the geometric initial-data convention, let $(M,g)$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold and let $\iota:\Sigma\hookrightarrow M$ be a smooth embedded three-manifold whose induced metric $h:=\iota^*g$ is positive definite. Its future unit normal $n$ satisfies $g(n,n)=-1$ and $g(n,X)=0$ for $X\in T\Sigma$. The second fundamental form is $K(X,Y):=g(\nabla_Xn,Y)$, with $\nabla$ the Levi-Civita connection of $g$ and the curvature sign convention stated in the Definition references section. The end data below are specified as a Riemannian metric and a symmetric tensor of these types; no embedding or Einstein constraint equation is required.

Let $E=\{x\in\mathbb R^3:r>R_0\}$, where $R_0>0$ is a length, $x=(x^1,x^2,x^3)$ are Cartesian coordinates measured in metres, and $r:=\sqrt{(x^1)^2+(x^2)^2+(x^3)^2}$. Write $\delta:=\delta_{ij}\,dx^i dx^j$ for the standard Euclidean metric, where $\delta_{ij}=1$ if $i=j$ and $0$ otherwise; repeated spatial indices are summed over $1,2,3$. A **fixed-chart asymptotically Euclidean end** consists of this exterior domain, a $C^2$ symmetric positive-definite covariant $2$-tensor $h=h_{ij}\,dx^i dx^j$, and a $C^1$ symmetric covariant $2$-tensor $K=K_{ij}\,dx^i dx^j$ such that
$$h_{ij}(x)=\delta_{ij}+\frac{a_{ij}}{r}+\rho_{ij}(x),\qquad K_{ij}(x)=O_1(r^{-2}),$$
where $a_{ij}=a_{ji}$ is a constant real matrix, $\epsilon>0$, and $\rho=O_2(r^{-1-\epsilon})$. For any tensor components $T_{ij}$, the notation $T=O_k(r^{-q})$ means that for every multi-index $\alpha=(\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\alpha_3)$ with $|\alpha|:=\alpha_1+\alpha_2+\alpha_3\le k$ there are constants $C_\alpha,R_\alpha$ such that $|\partial^\alpha T_{ij}(x)|\le C_\alpha r^{-q-|\alpha|}$ for $r\ge R_\alpha$, uniformly in angle. Thus the definition requires two Cartesian derivatives of the metric remainder and one of $K$. The coordinates and $r$ have units of metres; $\delta_{ij}$ and $h_{ij}$ are dimensionless, $a_{ij}$ has units of metres, and $K$ has inverse-length units in a spatial orthonormal frame.

For $R>R_0$, the coordinate sphere $S_R:=\{x:r=R\}$ is a smooth embedded surface in $E$. Let $\jmath_R:S_R\hookrightarrow E$ be its inclusion and $\gamma_R:=\jmath_R^*\delta$ its induced Riemannian metric. The Euclidean area measure $dS$ is the Riemannian area measure of $\gamma_R$: for any smooth rank-two local parametrization $X:U\subseteq\mathbb R^2\to S_R$ with coordinates $(y^1,y^2)$, its coordinate density is
$$dS=\sqrt{\det\bigl[\delta(\partial_{y^a}X,\partial_{y^b}X)\bigr]_{a,b=1}^{2}}\,dy^1dy^2.$$

The change-of-variables formula makes this density independent of the chosen surface coordinates; since $x$ is measured in metres, $dS$ has units of square metres. The sphere's outward Euclidean unit normal has components $n^i:=x^i/R$. If its limiting integral exists as $R\to\infty$—the spatial-infinity limit in this chosen chart—the **fixed-chart ADM energy** and its associated mass are
$$E_{\mathrm{ADM}}(h;x):=\frac{c^4}{16\pi G_N}\lim_{R\to\infty}\int_{S_R}\bigl(\partial_jh_{ij}-\partial_ih_{jj}\bigr)n^i\,dS,\qquad M_{\mathrm{ADM}}:=\frac{E_{\mathrm{ADM}}}{c^2}.$$
Here $c>0$ is the SI speed-of-light conversion constant with units metres per second, and $G_N>0$ is the Newtonian gravitational conversion constant with units metres cubed per kilogram per second squared. The limit has units of metres, $E_{\mathrm{ADM}}$ has units of joules, and $M_{\mathrm{ADM}}$ has units of kilograms. The prefactor fixes the asymptotic time-translation normalization; in SI coordinates use $x^0=ct$. No rescaling of this convention is part of the definition.

references.title: Eric Gourgoulhon, 3+1 Formalism and Bases of Numerical Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/0703035v1 (2007), §§7.2.1–7.2.2 and 7.3.1–7.3.2, PDF pp. 103–110; geometric units are used.
Sebastiano Bernuzzi, Lecture Notes on 3+1 Numerical Relativity, v0.1 (2021), §§7.1–7.2 and §7.2.2, PDF pp. 32–35; geometric units are used.
José Luis Jaramillo, Juan Antonio Valiente Kroon, and Eric Gourgoulhon, From Geometry to Numerics, arXiv:0712.2332v2 (2008), §2.1 and equation (2), PDF pp. 7–8.

items.title: Scalar curvature of a conformally Euclidean three-metric
items.design_state: Step 1 authoring complete draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.physical_scope: A local differential-geometric identity for a Riemannian metric; it asserts no Einstein constraint or physical model.
items.statement:
Let $E\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a nonempty open set with Cartesian coordinates $x^1,x^2,x^3$, standard Euclidean metric $\delta=\delta_{ij}\,dx^i dx^j$ with $\delta_{ij}=1$ for $i=j$ and $0$ otherwise, inverse components $\delta^{ij}$, and Laplacian $\Delta_\delta=\sum_{i=1}^3\partial_i^2$. Let $u\in C^\infty(E,(0,\infty))$ and set $h=u^4\delta$. Form the product Lorentzian manifold $\widehat M=\mathbb R_\tau\times E$ with metric $g=-d\tau^2+h$ and future orientation $\partial_\tau$; its slice $\Sigma=\{0\}\times E$ is a smooth spacelike hypersurface with induced metric $h$. Use the induced connection $D$ and curvature convention supplied for this slice by the earlier normal-decomposition theorem. In Cartesian coordinates define $R^\ell{}_{bcd}$ by $R(\partial_c,\partial_d)\partial_b=R^\ell{}_{bcd}\partial_\ell$, $\operatorname{Ric}^h_{ij}:=R^k{}_{ikj}$, and $S_h:=h^{ij}\operatorname{Ric}^h_{ij}$. For $f=2\log u$, write $|df|_\delta^2:=\delta^{ij}(\partial_i f)(\partial_j f)$. Then
$$S_h=-8u^{-5}\Delta_\delta u.$$

This statement concerns a smooth positive conformal metric and its induced scalar curvature. The product construction only fixes the geometric convention; no Einstein equation, energy condition, or completeness hypothesis is imposed.

references.title: Eric Gourgoulhon, 3+1 Formalism and Bases of Numerical Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/0703035v1 (2007), §§6.3.1–6.3.2, equations (6.48)–(6.52), PDF pp. 89–91.
Sebastiano Bernuzzi, Lecture Notes on 3+1 Numerical Relativity, v0.1 (2021), §6.3, equation (6.17), PDF pp. 26–27.

items.title: ADM energy of a conformally flat end
items.design_state: Step 1 authoring complete draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.physical_scope: A fixed-chart calculation for a conformally flat end; no constraint equation, positivity result, or empirical claim is inferred.
items.statement:
On a fixed-chart end $E=\{x\in\mathbb R^3:r=|x|>R_0\}$ with the ADM convention stated below, let $u\in C^\infty(E,(0,\infty))$ satisfy $u=1+m/(2r)+\rho$, where $m\in\mathbb R$ has units of metres and $\rho=O_2(r^{-2})$. Set $h=u^4\delta$ and choose any $C^1$ symmetric tensor $K=O_1(r^{-2})$. Then the ADM limit exists in the specified chart and
$$E_{\mathrm{ADM}}(h;x)=\frac{c^4m}{G_N}.$$

references.title: Eric Gourgoulhon, 3+1 Formalism and Bases of Numerical Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/0703035v1 (2007), §§7.3.1–7.3.2, equations (7.14)–(7.15) and (7.45)–(7.48), PDF pp. 105–110.
Sebastiano Bernuzzi, Lecture Notes on 3+1 Numerical Relativity, v0.1 (2021), §§7.2 and 7.2.2, equations (7.6b)–(7.6d) and (7.18)–(7.22), PDF pp. 33–35.
José Luis Jaramillo, Juan Antonio Valiente Kroon, and Eric Gourgoulhon, From Geometry to Numerics, arXiv:0712.2332v2 (2008), §2.1, equation (2), PDF pp. 7–8.

items.title: Compact interior changes leave a fixed ADM integral unchanged
items.design_state: Step 1 authoring complete draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.physical_scope: A fixed-chart equality of asymptotic limits under compactly supported metric changes; no field equation or positivity result is used.
items.statement:
Let $h$ and $h'$ be two $C^2$ Riemannian metrics on the same end $E=\{x\in\mathbb R^3:r=|x|>R_0\}$, with the same fixed Cartesian chart and asymptotic time normalization stated below. Suppose $h=h'$ outside a compact set $C\subset E$ and both fixed-chart ADM limits exist. Then
$$E_{\mathrm{ADM}}(h;x)=E_{\mathrm{ADM}}(h';x).$$
The symmetric tensors $K$ associated with the two data sets may differ; each need only satisfy the decay in the definition.

references.title: Eric Gourgoulhon, 3+1 Formalism and Bases of Numerical Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/0703035v1 (2007), §§7.2.1 and 7.3.1, equations (7.13)–(7.15), PDF pp. 103–106.
Sebastiano Bernuzzi, Lecture Notes on 3+1 Numerical Relativity, v0.1 (2021), §§7.1–7.2, equations (7.1a)–(7.6c), PDF pp. 32–34.
José Luis Jaramillo, Juan Antonio Valiente Kroon, and Eric Gourgoulhon, From Geometry to Numerics, arXiv:0712.2332v2 (2008), §2.1 and equation (2), PDF pp. 7–8.

title: Asymptotic ends and ADM surface integrals — Examples

items.title: The isotropic Schwarzschild end has energy Mc squared
items.design_state: Step 1 authoring complete draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.physical_scope: A fixed-chart calculation on the standard isotropic Schwarzschild slice data; no positive-mass theorem or empirical statement is asserted.
items.statement:
Let $M>0$ be a mass in kilograms and put $m=G_NM/c^2$, a length. On the end $E=\{x\in\mathbb R^3:r=|x|>m/2\}$, take the standard isotropic Schwarzschild slice data
$$u=1+\frac{m}{2r},\qquad h=u^4\delta,\qquad K=0.$$
Here “time-symmetric” means precisely $K=0$. With the fixed Cartesian end chart and unit asymptotic time normalization $x^0=ct$, the ADM energy is $Mc^2$ joules.

references.title: Eric Gourgoulhon, 3+1 Formalism and Bases of Numerical Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/0703035v1 (2007), §8.2.5, equations (8.63)–(8.64), and §7.3.2, equations (7.45)–(7.48), PDF pp. 109 and 133–134.
Sebastiano Bernuzzi, Lecture Notes on 3+1 Numerical Relativity, v0.1 (2021), §7.2, Example 7.2.2, equations (7.9)–(7.10), PDF pp. 33–34.
José Luis Jaramillo, Juan Antonio Valiente Kroon, and Eric Gourgoulhon, From Geometry to Numerics, arXiv:0712.2332v2 (2008), §2.1, equation (2), PDF pp. 7–8.

items.title: A compact interior change preserves the ADM limit but changes scalar curvature
items.design_state: Step 1 authoring complete draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.physical_scope: A smooth Riemannian metric example on a fixed asymptotic end; no Einstein constraint, completeness, or physical-solution claim is made.
items.statement:
Fix a length $R_0>0$, set $E=\{x\in\mathbb R^3:|x|>R_0\}$, and let $x_*=(3R_0,0,0)$. Define
$$\phi(x)=\begin{cases}\exp\!\left(-\frac{1}{1-|x-x_*|^2/R_0^2}\right),&|x-x_*|<R_0,\\0,&|x-x_*|\ge R_0.\end{cases}$$
For $0<\varepsilon<1$, set $u_0=1$, $u_\varepsilon=1+\varepsilon\phi$, $h_0=u_0^4\delta$, $h_\varepsilon=u_\varepsilon^4\delta$, and $K_0=K_\varepsilon=0$ on $E$. Both data sets have the same fixed-chart ADM energy, $0$, but their scalar curvatures differ at $x_*$.

references.title: Eric Gourgoulhon, 3+1 Formalism and Bases of Numerical Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/0703035v1 (2007), §6.3.2, equation (6.52), and §§7.3.1–7.3.2, equations (7.14)–(7.15), PDF pp. 90–91 and 105–110.
Sebastiano Bernuzzi, Lecture Notes on 3+1 Numerical Relativity, v0.1 (2021), §6.3, equation (6.17), and §7.2, equation (7.6c), PDF pp. 26–27 and 33–34.
José Luis Jaramillo, Juan Antonio Valiente Kroon, and Eric Gourgoulhon, From Geometry to Numerics, arXiv:0712.2332v2 (2008), §2.1, equation (2), PDF pp. 7–8.
